language.script_notes: Spanish and the Indigenous Guaraní are both official, and Guaraní is spoken by most of the population, so Guaraní words and the letters ñ, ý and g̃ can appear on signs and shops alongside Spanish. Street suffixes: Calle, Avenida, Ruta.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Bollards are not a strong national tell and are relatively uncommon.
road_furniture.line_paint: White edge lines with yellow center lines where roads are marked; many rural roads are unpaved.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted or plain kerbs in towns; red dirt roads outside cities.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Arch-shaped signboards spanning the road, rarely seen outside this country. Utility poles have cut-outs similar to Brazil's, and road signs have black backs, as in Brazil.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched clay tile roofs, often on courtyard-style houses; corrugated metal on newer buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Red brick made from the local clay is the defining material, along with timber and local stone; Spanish colonial and Baroque buildings in red and yellow tones; Jesuit mission ruins in dark red brick (a UNESCO World Heritage site); simple ranch (estancia) buildings on Mennonite farms in the north-west.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Red brick, ochre and yellow plaster, and whitewashed walls.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colonial and neoclassical buildings in the capital's historic center; Jesuit mission ruins near Encarnación; Mennonite ranches with grazing cattle in the Chaco; ñandutí lace as a national craft symbol.

nature.vegetation: Soybean, rice and corn fields in the wetter southeast; cotton and peanut farming and thorny dry forest (the Chaco) in the drier northwest; subtropical forest along the rivers; cattle pasture almost everywhere.
nature.terrain: A landlocked country divided by a great north-south river — hilly, fertile, red-soiled country in the east and a vast, flat, sparsely populated lowland plain (the Gran Chaco) in the west.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid subtropical climate; striking red soil in the east, and drier, scrubbier country toward the northwest.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur plate since 2019, with a blue band at the top carrying the country name, flag and Mercosur logo; the plates look slightly red-tinted in Street View compared with neighbours'.
vehicles.plate_format: Letters followed by digits on the white Mercosur plate.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorcycles are the primary personal transport, mostly imported from China and locally assembled; used Japanese and Korean cars fill the roads.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated in the east around the capital, Ciudad del Este and Encarnación; the northwest Chaco has limited coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared utility poles with cut-outs, road signs with black backs, red soil and soybean farms near the eastern border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Spanish and Guaraní signage rather than Portuguese; arch-shaped signboards over the road and the slightly red-tinted Mercosur plates are found here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Mercosur plates, Spanish signage and subtropical farmland in the north of Argentina
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Argentina's black Gen 3 car, chevron and kilometer markers differ; arch-shaped road signs and Guaraní words point here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Chaco lowlands and dry thorn scrub in the northwest
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bolivia's thick lumber utility poles and faint-blue plates differ, and the eastern hills and red soil are found here.
